catalogSnapshot.source: one SELECT from pg_catalog plus pg_policies; no business rows, DDL or DML
catalogSnapshot.query:
SELECT jsonb_build_object(
 'collected_at', statement_timestamp(),
 'server_version', current_setting('server_version'),
 'public_tables', COALESCE((
  SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
   'schema', n.nspname, 'table', c.relname,
   'rls_enabled', c.relrowsecurity, 'rls_forced', c.relforcerowsecurity,
   'anon_select', has_table_privilege('anon', c.oid, 'SELECT'),
   'anon_insert', has_table_privilege('anon', c.oid, 'INSERT'),
   'anon_update', has_table_privilege('anon', c.oid, 'UPDATE'),
   'anon_delete', has_table_privilege('anon', c.oid, 'DELETE'),
   'authenticated_select', has_table_privilege('authenticated', c.oid, 'SELECT'),
   'authenticated_insert', has_table_privilege('authenticated', c.oid, 'INSERT'),
   'authenticated_update', has_table_privilege('authenticated', c.oid, 'UPDATE'),
   'authenticated_delete', has_table_privilege('authenticated', c.oid, 'DELETE')
  ) ORDER BY n.nspname, c.relname)
  FROM pg_catalog.pg_class c JOIN pg_catalog.pg_namespace n ON n.oid=c.relnamespace
  WHERE n.nspname='public' AND c.relkind IN ('r','p')
 ), '[]'::jsonb),
 'public_policies', COALESCE((
  SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
   'schema', schemaname, 'table', tablename, 'policy', policyname,
   'permissive', permissive, 'roles', roles, 'command', cmd,
   'using', qual, 'with_check', with_check
  ) ORDER BY schemaname, tablename, policyname)
  FROM pg_catalog.pg_policies WHERE schemaname='public'
 ), '[]'::jsonb),
 'public_views', COALESCE((
  SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
   'schema', n.nspname, 'view', c.relname, 'kind', c.relkind,
   'options', c.reloptions,
   'anon_select', has_table_privilege('anon', c.oid, 'SELECT'),
   'authenticated_select', has_table_privilege('authenticated', c.oid, 'SELECT')
  ) ORDER BY n.nspname, c.relname)
  FROM pg_catalog.pg_class c JOIN pg_catalog.pg_namespace n ON n.oid=c.relnamespace
  WHERE n.nspname='public' AND c.relkind IN ('v','m')
 ), '[]'::jsonb)
) AS metadata

sourceBoundaries.priorCrosscheckScope: Existing full saved crosscheck reused; four specifically relevant source files independently match current immutable main. This does not fingerprint production application/migration history.

limits: This is a historical observed snapshot from saved parent-collected provider/catalog responses, not a fresh check at packaging time.
Advisor observations at07:40, general catalog at07:43 and friendship key metadata at07:57 are separate, non-atomic snapshots. The Auth connection notice has no per-finding observed_at.

Catalog scope is public ordinary/partitioned tables, public policies and public ordinary/materialized views. Effective privilege booleans cover table-level SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE for anon/authenticated, including inherited grants; they do not cover column ACLs, other privileges, schema access, RPC/function ACLs, non-public objects or service-role access.
Policy-role PUBLIC is not itself a table privilege. No actual-account row-isolation, query-plan, sustained-load or application behavior test was executed.

All relevant observed auth.uid calls match individual FROM-free scalar SELECT forms. Cached linter literal matching is a source-visible discrepancy, not proof of the live provider revision or actual per-row query-plan cost.
The friendship helper is intentionally row-dependent and is not a request for blind wrapping/removal. The checked-in SQL regression was read, not rerun.

No row data, row count, empty-table state, migration ledger/application history, current function definition/ACL inventory, workload horizon, statistics-reset time or index dependency/plan evidence was queried in these inputs.
No application of migrations077-079 or owner approval is inferred. Old Nov18 function/migration claims in the original finding are not promoted into these separately scoped Nov19 inputs.
Unused-index information does not establish a safe drop. Fixed Auth max10 is configuration evidence only; no setting change was requested or made.
October group counts cannot identify changed table/index identities where the old summary omitted them. Absence of an October no-primary-key group does not prove a primary key existed then.
